class.name: FlowBlackboard
class.brief_description: The variable values of a running graph.
class.description: A [FlowBlackboard] stores the current values of the variables of a [FlowGraph] under their names. A playback of a graph owns one blackboard, or several playbacks share one to exchange state, for example quest or dialogue state. The declarations (name, type, default) are [FlowVariable]s in [member FlowGraph.variables]; the blackboard does not check names or types against them. [signal variable_changed] is emitted for every change, which lets a user interface follow the state. The blackboard is a [Resource], so it can be saved and loaded like one. [codeblocks] [gdscript] var blackboard := FlowBlackboard.new() blackboard.variable_changed.connect(func(name, value): print(name, " = ", value)) blackboard.set_variable("gold", 50) print(blackboard.get_variable("gold", 0)) # 50 print(blackboard.get_variable("silver", 0)) # 0 [/gdscript] [csharp] var blackboard = new FlowBlackboard(); blackboard.VariableChanged += (name, value) => GD.Print(name, " = ", value); blackboard.SetVariable("gold", 50); GD.Print(blackboard.GetVariable("gold", 0)); // 50 GD.Print(blackboard.GetVariable("silver", 0)); // 0 [/csharp] [/codeblocks]

method.name: get_variable
method.description: Returns the value of the variable [param name], or [param default] if there is no such variable.

method.name: get_variable_names
method.description: Returns the names of all variables that currently have a value.

method.name: has_variable
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the variable [param name] has a value.

method.name: remove_variable
method.description: Removes the variable [param name]. Does nothing if it has no value. Emits [signal variable_changed] with a [code]null[/code] value if the variable existed.

method.name: set_variable
method.description: Sets the value of the variable [param name] and emits [signal variable_changed]. An empty [param name] is an error and changes nothing.

members.member: All values, keyed by variable name. Assigning a dictionary replaces all values and does not emit [signal variable_changed]. Prefer [method set_variable] to change single values.

signal.name: variable_changed
signal.description: Emitted when [method set_variable] sets a value, and when [method remove_variable] removes one (then [param value] is [code]null[/code]).
